items.skill_note: The trap is "kept in reserve as an extra": a real sense of "spare", but nothing in this passage supports it.

items.passage: The court ruled that the company had violated the [spirit] of the regulation even though its actions satisfied every clause, since the rule's purpose was to protect downwind residents.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word "spirit" most nearly mean?
choice_notes: a sense this passage rules out
another common sense of the word
items.explanation: Contrasting the regulation's purpose with its literal clauses points to intended meaning, not a ghost or morale.
items.skill_note: The trap is "a ghost or supernatural being": a real sense of "spirit", but nothing in this passage supports it.

items.passage: Unless the appellate court intervenes, the injunction will [stand] through the end of the year, and the construction site will remain fenced and empty.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word "stand" most nearly mean?
choices: to be upright on the feet
choice_notes: another common sense of the word
a sense this passage rules out
items.explanation: An order that remains in force leaves the site empty, which is the 'hold valid' sense of 'stand'.
items.skill_note: The trap is "to be upright on the feet": a real sense of "stand", but nothing in this passage supports it.

items.passage: Nothing in the new rules appears to [stem] the flow of counterfeit parts into the port, according to inspectors who tested the system for six months.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word "stem" most nearly mean?
choices: a root word to which affixes attach
choice_notes: another common sense of the word
a sense this passage rules out
items.explanation: Inspectors testing whether the rules reduce the flow are asking about restriction, the 'stem the tide' sense.
items.skill_note: The trap is "the stalk of a plant": a real sense of "stem", but nothing in this passage supports it.

items.passage: The reservoir's surface was so [still] that the surveyors could read the graduations on the far staff gauge from a quarter mile away, without binoculars.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word "still" most nearly mean?
choice_notes: another common sense of the word
a sense this passage rules out
items.explanation: Reading a gauge reflected in water requires an unbroken surface, which is the 'motionless' sense.
items.skill_note: The trap is "up to this time": a real sense of "still", but nothing in this passage supports it.

items.passage: The obituary was assembled almost entirely from [stock] phrases, offering the customary tributes to kindness and vision without naming a single event in the man's life.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word "stock" most nearly mean?
choices: a supply of goods held for sale
choice_notes: a sense this passage rules out
another common sense of the word
items.explanation: Phrases used without reference to any actual event are unoriginal, the 'stock' sense of commonplace.
items.skill_note: The trap is "shares in a company": a real sense of "stock", but nothing in this passage supports it.

items.passage: Peat bogs [store] roughly twice as much carbon per hectare as the forests that replaced them, which is why draining a bog releases more than clearing a wood.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word "store" most nearly mean?
choices: to put something away for future use
choice_notes: another common sense of the word
a sense this passage rules out
items.explanation: Bogs holding carbon over centuries are accumulating it, the 'store' sense of retention, not a shop.
items.skill_note: The trap is "a shop that sells goods": a real sense of "store", but nothing in this passage supports it.

items.passage: The committee [struck] the disputed sentence from the final report and replaced it with a footnote acknowledging that the evidence was inconclusive.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word "struck" most nearly mean?
choice_notes: another common sense of the word
a sense this passage rules out
items.explanation: Replacing a sentence with a footnote means it was removed, the editorial sense of 'strike'.
items.skill_note: The trap is "to hit repeatedly": a real sense of "strike", but nothing in this passage supports it.

items.passage: The book is a [study] in institutional failure: four chapters on the same agency, each describing a reform that was announced, funded, and never carried out.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word "study" most nearly mean?
choices: a careful examination of a subject
a room set aside for reading
a preliminary sketch for a painting
choice_notes: another common sense of the word
a sense this passage rules out
items.explanation: Four chapters analyzing one agency make the book an examination, the noun sense of 'study'.
items.skill_note: The trap is "a room set aside for reading": a real sense of "study", but nothing in this passage supports it.

items.passage: A [score] of nesting pairs returned to the island this spring, up from just four in 1998, when the rats were finally removed and the burrows began to hold.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word "score" most nearly mean?
choices: to cut a groove into a surface
the points earned in a game
choice_notes: a sense this passage rules out
another common sense of the word
items.explanation: The contrast with 'just four' counts birds, so 'score' is the archaic numeral meaning twenty.
items.skill_note: The trap is "the points earned in a game": a real sense of "score", but nothing in this passage supports it.

items.passage: The judge [stayed] the order for ninety days to give the agency time to produce the documents it had withheld, a delay the plaintiffs did not oppose.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word "stayed" most nearly mean?
choice_notes: a sense this passage rules out
another common sense of the word
items.explanation: Giving the agency ninety days before the order takes effect is suspending it, not remaining somewhere.
items.skill_note: The trap is "to remain in a place": a real sense of "stay", but nothing in this passage supports it.

items.passage: Adding lime raises the pH of acidic soil and makes phosphorus available to roots. ______, fields that had failed for years began to yield within two seasons.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The improved yield follows from the changed soil chemistry, so the blank marks cause and effect; 'nevertheless' would signal a reversal that never occurs.
items.skill_note: 'As a result' and 'nevertheless' both sound formal. Only one claims the second fact was caused by the first.

items.passage: Bats navigate by emitting calls and reading the returning echoes. ______, some deep-sea fish sense the electrical fields of nearby prey, relying on a sense no human possesses.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Two unrelated animals are being compared as parallel cases of non-visual sensing, so the blank marks similarity.
items.skill_note: Different species and different senses, but the same underlying point: similarity survives a change of topic.

items.passage: The harbor silted up after the upstream forest was cleared for charcoal. ______, the customs house moved three miles inland, where its foundations still stand beside a wheat field.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The customs house relocation was caused by the silting, so the blank marks a result.
items.skill_note: Physical cause, institutional effect. 'However' is the trap for anyone reading two unrelated facts.

items.passage: The survey recorded the height of each tree and its distance from the road. ______, it noted whether the trunk showed signs of damage from vehicles.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A third measurement is added to two others, so the blank is additive.
items.skill_note: Three measurements from one survey are cumulative. Nothing is being contrasted or concluded.

items.passage: Marine animals with very different ancestors have converged on remarkably similar body shapes. ______, dolphins, ichthyosaurs, and tunas all arrived at a streamlined, torpedo-like form.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The three animals are examples of the convergence just described, so the blank introduces an illustration.
items.skill_note: A list of species after a general claim is an example, even when the list is long.

items.passage: The lake's level fell by four meters after the irrigation canal opened in 1962. ______, the reed beds that had sheltered spawning fish dried out within a decade.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The reed beds died because the water level dropped, so the blank marks an effect of the falling lake.
items.skill_note: The second sentence is caused by the first. 'Likewise' would make it a parallel case rather than a result.

items.passage: Some inventions arrive decades before anyone needs them. ______, a working fax machine was demonstrated in 1843, thirty-three years before the telephone was patented.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The 1843 machine is a case of the general claim, so the blank introduces an example.
items.skill_note: The date is startling, but it supports the claim rather than contradicting it.

items.passage: Workers poured the foundation in March. ______, the steel frame went up in six weeks, faster than the schedule allowed.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The frame went up after the foundation was poured, so the blank marks the next step in a construction sequence.
items.skill_note: Chronology: foundation, then frame. No contrast and no causation is asserted.

items.passage: The report recommends widening the sidewalk along the market frontage. ______, it urges the city to plant shade trees on the same block before the next summer.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A second recommendation is added to the first, so the blank is additive.
items.skill_note: Two recommendations, same direction. 'Consequently' would claim the trees follow from the wider sidewalk.

items.passage: The printing press cut the cost of a printed page by roughly ninety percent. ______, pamphlets that had circulated in hundreds began to circulate in tens of thousands.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The larger print runs were produced by the lower cost, so the blank marks cause and effect.
items.skill_note: Cheap pages, many copies. The second sentence is the economic consequence of the first.

items.passage: The city banned leaded gasoline in 1986. ______, average blood lead levels in children fell by more than half within five years.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The decline in blood lead followed the ban, so the blank marks a result of the policy.
items.skill_note: Policy then outcome. 'Similarly' would make the decline a parallel case rather than an effect.

items.passage: The first edition sold poorly and was remaindered within two years. ______, the second, issued with a new preface and a lower price, went through four printings in a single year.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second edition's success reverses the first edition's failure, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: Same book, opposite outcomes. The later success is not caused by the earlier failure.

items.passage: The law requires inspectors to file a report within ten days of every site visit. ______, it obliges them to publish those reports on a public website within thirty.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A second obligation is added to the first, so the blank is additive.
items.skill_note: Two duties in one statute. Neither causes the other.

items.passage: The earliest telescopes used glass lenses, which had to be ground to a curve and mounted at both ends of a tube. ______, reflecting telescopes used a mirror that could be supported from behind, allowing far larger instruments.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Two designs are set against each other, so the blank marks contrast between them; the second does not follow from the first.
items.skill_note: Same purpose, different engineering. The comparison is oppositional, not additive.

items.passage: The volcano ejected ash into the stratosphere, where it reflected sunlight for eighteen months. ______, global temperatures fell by half a degree the following year.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The temperature drop was produced by the reflective ash, so the blank marks an effect.
items.skill_note: A physical mechanism links the two sentences. 'Nevertheless' would deny the link.

items.passage: The diet reduced systolic blood pressure by six points across the twelve-week trial. ______, it lowered LDL cholesterol by nearly twelve percent, an effect the researchers had not predicted.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A second measured benefit is added to the first, so the blank is additive.
items.skill_note: Two independent benefits, same direction. The cholesterol result is not an example of the blood-pressure result.

items.passage: Termites cultivate fungi in chambers they build from chewed wood, feeding the fungus and eating its crops in return. ______, leafcutter ants farm a different fungus, in gardens they weed and prune like farmers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Two insect lineages are compared as parallel cases of agriculture, so the blank marks similarity.
items.skill_note: Different insects, different fungi, same relationship. Similarity is the point.

items.passage: The dam trapped the sediment that had once replenished the delta each spring. ______, the delta shrank by nearly a kilometer a year, and the fishing villages at its edge moved inland twice.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The shrinking delta follows from the trapped sediment, so the blank marks a consequence.
items.skill_note: Sediment starvation causes coastal loss. The cause is physical, not logical.

items.passage: The first movement of the quartet is in a bright major key and lasts barely four minutes. ______, the second movement is in the parallel minor and stretches past eleven, with a theme that never resolves.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second movement contrasts with the first in key, mood, and length, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: Two movements described in opposite terms. The second does not follow from the first.

items.passage: The archive contains forty thousand photographs of the construction. ______, it holds nine hundred hours of audio recordings made by the site engineer.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The audio recordings are a second collection added to the photographs, so the blank is additive.
items.skill_note: Two holdings, one archive. Addition is the only relation asserted.

items.passage: Certain species cannot reproduce without fire. ______, the jack pine produces cones that open only when the resin sealing them has been melted by intense heat.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The jack pine is one species exhibiting the dependence just described, so the blank introduces an example.
items.skill_note: A general claim about 'certain species' is followed by one named species.

items.passage: The clay was first wedged to remove air pockets, then shaped on a wheel and left to dry for two days. ______, it was fired in a wood kiln for thirty hours.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Firing follows drying in the potter's sequence, so the blank marks the next step.
items.skill_note: A procedural sequence with clear stages.

items.passage: The 1880s guidebook recommends the coastal route as safe for families and passable in any weather. ______, the 1902 edition warns that the same path is impassable after rain and has drowned four travelers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The later edition reverses the earlier assessment, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: Two editions of one guidebook, opposite advice.

items.passage: The first-year students improved their reading speed by forty words per minute. ______, their comprehension scores did not change at all.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Unchanged comprehension qualifies the improvement in speed, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: A gain in one measure and no gain in another. The second sentence limits the first.

items.passage: The city's trees cool the streets in summer by shading pavement and releasing water vapor. ______, they intercept rainfall that would otherwise overwhelm storm drains.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A second service performed by the same trees is added, so the relation is additive.
items.skill_note: One object, two benefits. Neither benefit causes the other.

items.passage: The first attempt to measure the mountain's height used a chain stretched across a valley and gave a figure four hundred meters too low. ______, a second attempt using triangulation from three valleys came within twelve meters of the modern value.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second survey came after the first and replaced its figure, so the blank marks a later stage.
items.skill_note: Two attempts in sequence, the second correcting the first.

items.passage: Road crews spread salt by the ton every winter to keep the passes open. ______, chloride concentrations in the valley's wells have tripled since 1990, and three municipal supplies now exceed the safety threshold.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The rising chloride follows from the salt applications, so the blank marks an effect.
items.skill_note: Salt on roads, chloride in wells. A direct physical pathway, not a coincidence to be contrasted.

items.passage: The statute sets a minimum wage for all hourly workers in the state. ______, it requires employers to pay time and a half for any hour beyond forty in a week.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A second requirement is added to the first, so the blank is additive.
items.skill_note: Two provisions of one statute, same direction. Neither is a consequence of the other.

items.passage: The museum lends objects only to institutions that can guarantee climate control in transit and on display. ______, it requires borrowers to insure the work at full replacement value for the entire loan period.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A second condition is added to the first, so the blank is additive.
items.skill_note: Two loan conditions, side by side.

items.passage: The 1858 expedition mapped the strait but lost its supply cache to a storm and turned back within forty miles of the open water. ______, a second expedition in 1871 reached the same point with dogs and crossed in nine days.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The 1871 expedition came thirteen years after the first, so the blank marks a later attempt.
items.skill_note: Two expeditions in sequence, the second succeeding where the first failed.

items.passage: Dredging deepened the shipping channel by three meters but removed the gravel beds where smelt had spawned. ______, the commercial catch of smelt fell by ninety percent over the following six years.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The catch collapse follows from the loss of spawning habitat, so the blank marks a consequence.
items.skill_note: Habitat destroyed, fishery collapsed. The second fact is caused by the first.

items.passage: Reviewers praised the exhibition's scholarship and the clarity of its labels. ______, visitors interviewed at the exit described the galleries as crowded, poorly lit, and hard to navigate.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Visitor complaints stand against the reviewers' praise, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: Two audiences, two verdicts. The visitors' view is not caused by the reviewers'.

items.passage: The baker mixes the flour and water and leaves them for an hour before adding salt or yeast. ______, she folds the dough every forty minutes for the next three hours.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Folding follows the resting period in the baking sequence, so the blank marks the next step.
items.skill_note: Procedural order: rest, then fold.

items.passage: The city replaced its lead service lines over eleven years, beginning in the poorest districts. ______, the share of children with elevated blood lead fell from thirty percent to under two.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The decline in blood lead followed the pipe replacement, so the blank marks a result.
items.skill_note: Infrastructure replaced, exposure fell. Physical cause and effect.

items.passage: The collection includes the composer's handwritten scores and his annotated copies of other people's music. ______, it holds the only surviving recording of his own piano playing, made on a wax cylinder in 1904.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A third category of material is added, so the blank is additive.
items.skill_note: Three kinds of holding in one archive.

items.passage: A single base change in the gene replaces one amino acid in the enzyme's active site. ______, the enzyme loses almost all of its catalytic activity at body temperature.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The loss of activity is caused by the substitution, so the blank marks an effect.
items.skill_note: Molecular change, functional consequence.

items.passage: The 1890 edition lists eleven species of warbler in the county. ______, the 2020 survey found only six, and two of those were represented by a single breeding pair each.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The later count is set against the earlier one, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: Two surveys 130 years apart, opposite results.

items.passage: City foresters once planted a single species along each street, on the theory that uniformity simplified maintenance. ______, the Dutch elm disease epidemic of the 1930s showed that one species can vanish from an entire city in a decade.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence contradicts the theory of the first, so the blank needs a contrast transition; 'therefore' would make the epidemic a consequence of uniformity, and the other two misstate the relation.
items.skill_note: The first sentence states a belief, the second undermines it. Any causal or additive transition reverses the logic.

items.passage: The treaty ceded the island's fishing rights to the mainland government for ninety-nine years. ______, it required the departing administration to keep the lighthouse lantern in working order.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Both sentences list separate terms of the same treaty, so the blank adds a second provision rather than contrasting or explaining one.
items.skill_note: Two clauses from one document are parallel, not opposed. 'By contrast' is the trap for readers who see two different topics.

items.passage: Some bureaucratic records outlast the institutions that produced them. ______, the Venice plague returns, which record every death in the city between 1576 and 1577, survive while the health board that compiled them does not.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The Venice returns are one instance of the general claim, so the blank introduces an example; 'thus' would wrongly present the instance as a consequence.
items.skill_note: A general statement followed by one named case is exemplification, not proof by consequence.

items.passage: The monks copied the text in the eleventh century, leaving wide margins on every page. ______, a reader filled those margins with notes in a hand datable to the 1300s.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The marginal notes were added after the copying, so the blank marks a later point in time; 'meanwhile' would wrongly make the two acts simultaneous.
items.skill_note: Paleography dates the two hands three centuries apart. Sequence, not simultaneity.

items.passage: Nineteenth-century critics dismissed the novel as melodrama and predicted it would be forgotten within a year. ______, it sold more copies in its first twelve months than any book the publisher had ever handled.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The commercial success stands against the prediction, so the blank marks contrast; 'therefore' would make sales a consequence of dismissal.
items.skill_note: A prediction followed by its refutation is contrast, even when both sentences are about the same book.

items.passage: The first census counted 4,100 residents in the town. ______, a second count ten years later recorded 3,900, the only decline in the town's recorded history.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second count happened ten years after the first, so the blank marks a later event in a sequence.
items.skill_note: 'Meanwhile' would claim the two counts happened at once; the dates forbid it.

items.passage: Lichens absorb nutrients directly through their surfaces and are killed by sulfur dioxide at concentrations far below human tolerance. ______, their absence from a city block is a reliable indicator of air quality.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The indicator value follows from the lichens' sensitivity, so the blank marks a conclusion drawn from the fact stated.
items.skill_note: Sensitivity to a pollutant produces an inference about air quality. That is causation in the reasoning, not contrast.

items.passage: The archive holds the correspondence of three generations of the family. ______, it preserves the only surviving copy of their account books, which record every harvest from 1702 to 1789.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The account books are a second holding added to the correspondence, so the blank is additive and intensifying.
items.skill_note: Two kinds of document in one archive: addition. The account books are not an instance of correspondence.

items.passage: The algorithm performs well on the data it was trained on. ______, its accuracy falls by half when it is applied to records from a different hospital.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Strong training performance is set against poor performance elsewhere, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: One strength and one failure of the same system. The second clause limits the first rather than following from it.

items.passage: Most desert plants close their pores during the day to conserve water. ______, the creosote bush keeps them open at dawn, when the air is humid enough to offset the loss.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The creosote bush behaves differently from the general pattern, so the blank marks contrast with that pattern.
items.skill_note: 'Most' invites an exception. An exception is a contrast, not an additional example of the rule.

items.passage: Colonial administrators frequently misread local property arrangements. ______, a survey of Bengal in 1793 recorded a single owner for land that three families had farmed jointly for generations.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The Bengal survey is one documented case of the general misreading, so the blank introduces an example.
items.skill_note: The survey is evidence of the claim, not a consequence of it.

items.passage: The comet was first spotted in 1786 and then lost to view. ______, it was rediscovered in 1795, within a degree of where an orbit calculation had predicted it would be.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The rediscovery came nine years later, so the blank marks a later point in the narrative.
items.skill_note: A gap of nine years is sequence. 'Meanwhile' would collapse the gap.

items.passage: The theory predicts that heavier isotopes of oxygen should evaporate more slowly and therefore be rarer in ancient rainfall. ______, the isotope ratios in the ice core show the opposite pattern at every depth sampled.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The measured pattern contradicts the prediction, so the blank marks an unexpected reversal.
items.skill_note: A prediction and a contrary measurement. The measurement does not follow from the theory.

items.passage: The cathedral's vaults required an estimated 12,000 oak trees. ______, the scaffolding alone consumed another 4,000, stripped from forests forty miles away.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A second quantity is added to the first to show the total scale of timber use, so the blank is additive.
items.skill_note: Both figures measure the same thing. Addition, not contrast.

items.passage: Institutions often preserve the paperwork of decisions they would rather forget. ______, the East India Company's archive retains an inventory of a cargo it later claimed never to have shipped.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The inventory is a documented instance of the general claim, so the blank introduces an example.
items.skill_note: 'Often' announces a pattern; one company archive illustrates it.

items.passage: While the northern fleet blockaded the harbor, the southern army advanced inland along the river road. ______, a third force was crossing the mountains, unseen by either side.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The third force acted at the same time as the other two, so the blank marks simultaneity.
items.skill_note: Three simultaneous movements. Any causal or summarizing transition breaks the timeline.

items.passage: The result was not what anyone in the lab had expected. ______, the control group outperformed the group that received the training.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The reversal is the content of the surprise, so the blank introduces the specific fact that makes the result unexpected.
items.skill_note: 'Not what anyone expected' sets up the revelation that follows.

items.passage: The northern dialect preserves the older vowel system almost intact. ______, the southern dialect has merged two vowels that remain distinct everywhere else in the language.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Two dialects are set against each other on the same feature, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: A single linguistic feature, two opposite outcomes.

items.passage: Many colonial-era maps of the interior were drawn from travelers' hearsay rather than survey. ______, a 1752 chart labels a mountain range that no European expedition had yet seen.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The 1752 chart is a documented case of the general claim, so the blank introduces an example.
items.skill_note: 'Rather than survey' predicts exactly this kind of error, so the second sentence confirms rather than contradicts.

items.passage: The letters were written over four years, from the first winter of the siege to the spring after it. ______, they were bundled with string and hidden inside a wall, where a mason found them in 1931.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The hiding happened after the letters were written, so the blank marks a later event.
items.skill_note: Two moments separated by decades. The blank moves the narrative forward, not sideways.

items.passage: The settlement was not a small seasonal camp. ______, it covered forty hectares, held at least two hundred structures, and was occupied in every season of the year.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence escalates the first with evidence of size and permanence, which 'in fact' signals.
items.skill_note: 'Not a small camp' demands a denial of the smallness, not a contrast with it.

items.passage: The first set of soil samples was collected in January, when the ground was frozen to a depth of forty centimeters. ______, a second set was taken immediately after the spring melt.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sampling followed the first by months, so the blank marks a later stage.
items.skill_note: The samples were taken months apart, so the blank must move the account forward in time.

items.passage: Ottoman courts kept registers of property sales that name the buyer, the seller, the price, and the witnesses. ______, Venetian notaries recorded transactions in comparable detail, often adding the purpose of the purchase.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Two legal systems are compared as parallel record-keeping practices, so the blank marks similarity.
items.skill_note: Different empires, comparable practice. The Venetian detail does not contradict the Ottoman one.

items.passage: Between 1880 and 1900 the price of wheat fell by nearly a third. ______, the price of farmland in the same counties rose, driven by demand from speculators who expected railways.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Falling wheat prices are set against rising land prices, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: Two prices moving in opposite directions. 'Therefore' would falsely claim one caused the other.

items.passage: A single mutation changes one amino acid in the protein's binding site. ______, the virus can no longer be neutralized by antibodies raised against the earlier strain.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The loss of neutralization follows from the altered binding site, so the blank marks a consequence.
items.skill_note: A molecular change produces an immune consequence. The relation is causal.

items.passage: The survey found the orchid at twelve sites along the ridge. ______, it found evidence of flowering at only three of them, all within a single valley.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A second finding is added to the first, and the two are compatible: presence at twelve sites, flowering at three.
items.skill_note: Both sentences report results of the same survey. Addition, not qualification.

items.passage: Revolutionary governments standardized weights and measures to make tax collection predictable. ______, the decree of 1795 fixed the meter at one ten-millionth of the distance from pole to equator.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The 1795 decree is a documented instance of the general standardization, so the blank introduces an example.
items.skill_note: The decree exemplifies the policy; it is not an effect of it in the logical sense the blank requires.

items.passage: The loss was not gradual. ______, the entire colony vanished from the reef within a single summer, leaving bare coral skeleton where a dense thicket had stood in June.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence supplies the extreme rapidity that proves the loss was sudden, which 'in fact' introduces.
items.skill_note: 'Not gradual' needs evidence of suddenness, not a contrast with it.

items.passage: The mechanical clock allowed hours to be counted uniformly, regardless of the season or the length of daylight. ______, work schedules, market times, and wage contracts could be fixed in advance.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Predictable scheduling follows from uniform hours, so the blank marks a result.
items.skill_note: A technical change enables an administrative one. Cause and effect.

items.passage: The bats emerge from the cave at dusk in a dense column that lasts about twenty minutes. ______, they return at dawn singly or in pairs, over a period of nearly two hours.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The departure and the return are described as opposite patterns, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: Same animals, opposite behavior at the two ends of the night.

items.passage: The treaty's language about the river is deliberately vague. ______, it refers to 'the navigation of the said watercourse' without saying which bank, which season, or which vessels.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The quoted phrase is a specific illustration of the vagueness, so the blank introduces an example.
items.skill_note: The quotation demonstrates the claim; it is not a consequence of it.

items.passage: The choir's earliest recordings were made in a church with a seven-second reverberation. ______, every later recording was made in a studio with almost none, which critics said stripped the sound of its character.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The two recording conditions are set against each other, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: Two acoustic environments with opposite properties.

items.passage: The region receives less than ten centimeters of rain a year. ______, the vineyards there produce some of the most concentrated fruit in the country, because the roots reach groundwater twelve meters down.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The quality of the wine contradicts what the rainfall figure would predict, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: Scarcity of rain normally predicts poor vines; here it does not.

items.passage: The archive's cataloguing system was designed for paper letters and cannot describe a file that exists only as data. ______, a third of the collection is now effectively invisible to researchers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The invisibility of the digital third is caused by the mismatch between the catalog and the material, so the blank marks a consequence.
items.skill_note: An inadequate tool produces a gap in access.

items.passage: The soil in the treated plots held nearly twice as much water as the soil in the controls. ______, the plants in those plots survived a six-week drought that killed every control plant.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The survival follows from the greater water retention, so the blank marks a consequence.
items.skill_note: Water-holding capacity explains drought survival. Cause, not illustration.

items.passage: The biologist expected the introduced snail to outcompete the native species within a decade. ______, the native snail expanded its range upstream, into water the introduced species could not tolerate.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The outcome contradicts the expectation, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: A prediction followed by its opposite. 'Likewise' would make the expansion a second prediction rather than a reversal.

items.passage: Governments sometimes adopt policies chiefly for their symbolic value, knowing the practical effect will be small. ______, a ban on plastic straws in a city that incinerates its waste changes little, yet it signals a direction of travel.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The straw ban is an example of the general pattern, so the blank introduces an illustration.
items.skill_note: The example agrees with the claim, even though the policy is described as ineffective.

items.passage: The printer carved each page in reverse on a block of pear wood, inked the surface, and pressed it against damp paper. ______, the block was cleaned, dried, and stored for the next printing, sometimes decades later.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Cleaning and storing the block came after printing, so the blank marks the next stage in the process.
items.skill_note: A craft sequence: carve, ink, press, store.

items.passage: The editor's changes were not minor corrections of spelling and punctuation. ______, she cut two chapters, reordered three others, and rewrote the final paragraph entirely.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence shows how extensive the changes were, escalating beyond the minor-correction reading, which 'in fact' signals.
items.skill_note: 'Not minor' promises escalation; a contrast transition would cancel the escalation.

items.passage: Two independent dating methods, radiocarbon on the charcoal and luminescence on the surrounding sand, agreed to within a century. ______, the occupation of the site can be placed between 1100 and 1200 CE.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The agreement of two methods is compressed into a single conclusion, which 'in short' marks.
items.skill_note: Converging evidence then one date range: summary and inference.

items.passage: Warmer winters have shortened the period in which standing water freezes hard enough to kill insect larvae. ______, tick populations have expanded northward by nearly two hundred kilometers in three decades.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The northward expansion is a consequence of the milder winters, so the blank marks a result.
items.skill_note: Climate mechanism then population response. Cause and effect.

items.passage: Many burial rituals involve objects that were deliberately broken before interment. ______, at one Anglo-Saxon cemetery, nearly every spearhead in the graves had been bent at the socket.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The bent spearheads are a documented instance of the general practice, so the blank introduces an example.
items.skill_note: The cemetery confirms the pattern rather than contradicting it.

items.passage: The crater is not merely large. ______, its outer rim encloses an area greater than the entire metropolitan region, and the shock layer beneath it extends four kilometers down.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence amplifies the claim about size with two measurements, which 'indeed' marks.
items.skill_note: 'Not merely large' demands escalation, not contrast.

items.passage: The island's two dialects share a vocabulary for fishing that is almost identical. ______, both preserve a set of tide terms that the mainland languages lost centuries ago.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A second shared feature is presented as a parallel case, so the blank marks similarity.
items.skill_note: Two similarities, one after the other. Addition in substance, similarity in framing.

items.passage: The fire spread quickly because the warehouse held paper, the wind came off the river at thirty knots, and the sprinkler system had been disconnected for repairs. ______, the building's timber frame had been soaked in oil for decades.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A fourth contributing factor is added to three others, so the blank is additive.
items.skill_note: A list of causes continues. Nothing is being concluded or contrasted.

items.passage: The winner's time was fast for the course, but the margin was what startled the organizers. ______, the second-place runner finished nearly four minutes behind, the largest gap in the race's ninety-year history.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence specifies the startling margin, intensifying the claim, which 'in fact' signals.
items.skill_note: The detail is offered as proof of the margin's size, not as a contrast to it.

items.passage: Four independent laboratories dated the ash layer to the same century, using four different methods. ______, the eruption can be fixed to the 1150s with reasonable confidence.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The date follows from the agreement of four methods, so the blank marks an inference.
items.skill_note: Converging measurements produce a conclusion.

items.passage: Farmers in the northern valley planted wheat on the flatter fields and grazed sheep on the slopes. ______, those in the southern valley drained the marsh and planted rice, which needed twice the labor but yielded three times the calories.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Two valleys are set against each other in agricultural practice, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: Same period, different economies. The comparison is oppositional.

items.passage: A few languages have no words for left and right, relying instead on compass directions for every spatial description. ______, speakers of one such language will say that a spoon is 'northwest of the cup' rather than beside it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The spoon example illustrates the general claim, so the blank introduces an example.
items.skill_note: One named language demonstrates the pattern just described.

items.passage: The comet was observed continuously for eleven months before it passed behind the sun. ______, it reappeared on the far side almost exactly where the orbit calculation had placed it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The reappearance came after the passage behind the sun, so the blank marks a later event.
items.skill_note: A predicted reappearance confirms the orbit; the blank is chronological.

items.passage: The theory predicted that the isotope ratio would rise steadily with altitude. ______, the samples from the highest stations showed the lowest ratios of all.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The measured values contradict the prediction, so the blank marks a reversal.
items.skill_note: Prediction and contrary data. The data cannot be a consequence of the theory.

items.passage: The report documents the decline of the fishery in three chapters. ______, it proposes a licensing scheme, a closed season, and a buyback program for the largest trawlers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A set of recommendations is added to the diagnosis, so the blank is additive.
items.skill_note: Diagnosis then proposals: two parts of one report, not a contrast.

items.passage: Administrative forms often outlive the purposes they were designed to serve. ______, the census still asks for the number of chimney stacks, a question added in 1861 to assess a hearth tax repealed in 1889.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The chimney question is a documented case of the general claim, so the blank introduces an example.
items.skill_note: The repeal date shows the question is obsolete, which supports the claim rather than opposing it.

items.passage: The lighthouse was automated in 1983, and its keepers were reassigned to other stations. ______, the foghorn was switched off entirely, since satellite navigation had made it redundant.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The two changes occurred in the same period, so the blank marks simultaneity.
items.skill_note: Automation and the loss of the foghorn happened together, not one because of the other.

items.passage: The temperature rise at the poles is not a small effect. ______, it is nearly four times the global average, and the difference has grown since the 1990s.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence supplies the magnitude that proves the point, which 'in fact' introduces.
items.skill_note: 'Not a small effect' is completed by a large number.

items.passage: The city replaced its horse-drawn trams with electric ones between 1895 and 1900, and the number of passengers carried tripled in the same five years. ______, fare revenue rose fast enough to repay the cost of conversion within a decade.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The revenue recovery is presented as a result of the passenger growth, so the blank marks a consequence.
items.skill_note: More riders produce more fares. A contrast or comparison transition would deny the arithmetic link.

items.passage: The bridge was not merely repaired. ______, every cable was replaced, a job that required closing the crossing for two full years.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence intensifies the first by specifying a far larger intervention, which is the emphatic force of 'in fact'.
items.skill_note: 'Not merely' promises an escalation. A contrast transition would cancel the escalation instead of completing it.

items.passage: The excavation produced no coins, no pottery, and no bone; the stratigraphy was undisturbed from top to bottom. ______, the site had never been occupied.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence condenses the evidence into a conclusion, which is the summarizing function of 'in short'.
items.skill_note: A list of absences followed by a verdict is a summary, not an illustration of one item in the list.

items.passage: The vaccine's protection against infection wanes after about eight months. ______, it still prevents severe illness in most recipients, even when it fails to block the virus entirely.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence concedes the first point but limits its importance, which 'that said' signals; 'therefore' would draw a conclusion the data do not support.
items.skill_note: Concession plus a limiting clause. The second sentence does not follow from the first; it qualifies it.

items.passage: The effect was not subtle. ______, the treated plots produced three times the biomass of the controls, a difference visible from the road.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence strengthens the claim that the effect was obvious by giving a striking measurement, which 'indeed' signals.
items.skill_note: Emphasis, not example: the measurement is offered as confirmation of the scale, not as one case among many.

items.passage: The manuscript is undeniably beautiful, with gold leaf intact on nine of its twelve miniatures. ______, those miniatures were probably added a century after the text was copied.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence concedes the beauty but withdraws the inference a reader might draw from it, which 'even so' marks.
items.skill_note: Praise followed by a qualification is concession, not consequence.

items.passage: Nothing in the letter suggests panic. ______, the writer describes the fire in the same flat tone he uses for the price of coal.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence supports the claim about tone with the strongest available evidence, which is emphatic confirmation.
items.skill_note: The evidence points the same way as the claim. A contrast transition would imply the letter does show panic.

items.passage: Roman concrete in the harbor moles has outlasted modern portland cement exposed to the same seawater for eighteen centuries. ______, some twentieth-century piers a few hundred meters away are already crumbling.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The modern piers are measured against the Roman moles, so the blank sets up an explicit comparison.
items.skill_note: The point is relative durability. The crumbling pier is not an example of Roman concrete.

items.passage: The drought was severe by any measure. ______, the reservoir fell to eleven percent of capacity, a level not recorded since 1977.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The reservoir figure is offered as proof of the severity, intensifying rather than illustrating the claim.
items.skill_note: One dramatic number after a general claim: confirmation, not an example drawn from a class.

items.passage: The two accounts agree on the date, the weather, the number of ships, and the name of the harbor pilot. ______, they were probably written by people who spoke to the same witness.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The agreement across four details is condensed into a conclusion, which 'in short' signals.
items.skill_note: Listing shared details then drawing a single inference is summary.

items.passage: The map is beautifully drawn, internally consistent, and dated to the year it claims. ______, it places a navigable river where every other source puts a road.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence concedes the map's virtues but disqualifies it as a source, which 'even so' marks.
items.skill_note: Three compliments then one fatal flaw: concession, not addition.

items.passage: No treaty, no boundary marker, and no shared court records survive from the period. ______, the two villages had never formally defined where one ended and the other began.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The absence of any documentation is condensed into a conclusion about the boundary, which 'in short' marks.
items.skill_note: A list of absences followed by a single inference is summary.

items.passage: The drug is expensive, must be kept cold, and requires a nurse to administer it. ______, it cures the infection in nine cases out of ten, in a single dose.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence concedes the practical drawbacks but points to an overriding benefit, which 'that said' signals.
items.skill_note: Three drawbacks, then one decisive advantage. Concession, not causation.

items.passage: The gap between the two groups was larger than the researchers had predicted. ______, it widened at every one of the five sites, including the two where the treatment was weakest.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence confirms and strengthens the first by showing the pattern held everywhere, which 'indeed' marks.
items.skill_note: The detail does not illustrate one case of a class; it amplifies the surprising size of the effect.

items.passage: Three laboratories, using three different methods, obtained the same half-life to within two percent. ______, the measurement is unlikely to be an artifact of any one technique.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The agreement across methods supports an inference about reliability, so the blank marks a conclusion.
items.skill_note: Converging evidence licenses an inference. That is deduction, not illustration.

items.passage: The ruling settled which court had jurisdiction over the dispute. ______, it said nothing about the amount of damages owed, which required a second trial.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence limits what the ruling accomplished, so the blank marks contrast between what was settled and what was left open.
items.skill_note: A completed action followed by what it did not do is a contrast, not an addition.

items.passage: The recipe calls for the spices to be toasted whole before grinding. ______, the oils that carry their aroma are released only at high heat, and they evaporate quickly once the seed is broken.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence gives the precise mechanism behind the instruction, so the blank narrows to the specific reason.
items.skill_note: Toasting then grinding is the general instruction; the chemistry explains it in detail.

items.passage: The manuscript's paper contains no rag fibers, only wood pulp. ______, it cannot have been made before about 1870, when wood pulping became commercially viable.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The dating conclusion is forced by the paper's composition, so the blank marks an inference.
items.skill_note: Material evidence establishes a terminus post quem. That is deduction.

items.passage: The orchard's bees are rented by the week from a keeper three counties away. ______, a late frost that kills the blossoms strands the keeper with hives and the orchard with no second chance at pollination.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The shared vulnerability follows from the rental arrangement, so the blank marks a result of that dependence.
items.skill_note: One arrangement creates one risk. The frost's damage is caused by the dependency.

items.passage: The excavation's pottery came from a single kiln, its clay matched the local riverbed, and its shapes appear nowhere else in the region. ______, the ware was made on site rather than imported.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Three converging details are reduced to one conclusion, which 'in short' marks.
items.skill_note: Evidence listed, then compressed into a single inference.

items.passage: The novel's narrator contradicts himself three times in the first chapter. ______, the reader is never told whether the contradictions are carelessness or design.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The absence of explanation sits oddly against the contradictions, so the blank marks contrast with what the reader expects.
items.skill_note: Contradictions raise a question that the text then declines to answer.

items.passage: Conserving the painted ceiling requires scaffolding that costs more than the building's annual maintenance budget. ______, the pigments are flaking at a rate that will erase the central panel within twenty years.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence concedes the cost but argues the work cannot wait, which 'that said' signals.
items.skill_note: A prohibitive cost followed by a reason to pay it anyway is concession.

items.passage: A 2011 study of bilingual children found no disadvantage in vocabulary size at age five. ______, a 2019 study of the same cohort found that the bilingual group knew fewer words in each language than monolinguals, though more across both.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The later finding complicates and opposes the earlier one, so the blank marks contrast.
items.skill_note: Same cohort, different measurement, opposite headline. The second study is not an application of the first.

items.passage: The contract's delivery clause is ambiguous about who bears the cost of unloading. ______, it never states whether the seller's obligation ends at the dock or at the buyer's warehouse.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence narrows the ambiguity to one exact question, which 'specifically' marks.
items.skill_note: A general problem followed by its precise form is specification, not contrast.

items.passage: The sediment cores did not show the gradual change the model predicted. ______, they showed a shift from forest to grassland within a single centimeter of deposit, perhaps two decades.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence asserts something stronger than the first by quantifying the abruptness, which 'indeed' marks.
items.skill_note: 'Did not show gradual change' is completed by evidence of abrupt change.

items.passage: The seed pods burst open only when the humidity drops below thirty percent. ______, the species disperses its seeds in the dry season, when the ground is hard and the wind is steady.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The timing of dispersal follows from the humidity trigger, so the blank marks a consequence.
items.skill_note: A mechanical trigger explains the seasonal timing.

items.passage: Three lines of evidence, linguistic, genetic, and archaeological, point to a single migration from the mainland around 1200 CE. ______, the settlement of the islands was probably accomplished in one wave rather than several.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The three lines are condensed into one conclusion, which 'in short' marks.
items.skill_note: Convergent evidence, then a compressed inference.

items.passage: The compound binds to a receptor that exists in two slightly different forms, one in the lung and one in the heart. ______, the drug's usefulness depends entirely on how strongly it prefers the lung form.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The conclusion about the drug's usefulness follows from the two receptor forms, so the blank marks an inference.
items.skill_note: Selectivity between two forms determines whether the drug is usable.

items.passage: Monitoring the colony requires a permit, a helicopter charter, and two trained observers for a full week each season. ______, the population has been counted every year since 1978 without a single gap.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence concedes the cost but points to an unbroken record, which 'that said' signals.
items.skill_note: Expense acknowledged, achievement asserted. Not a consequence of the expense.

items.passage: The tests detected the compound in no sample, the instruments were calibrated twice, and the reagent was fresh. ______, the contamination must have occurred before the samples reached the lab.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The conclusion about when contamination happened is inferred from the three clean facts, so the blank marks an inference.
items.skill_note: Eliminating every lab-side explanation forces a conclusion. That is deduction, not contrast.

items.passage: Admittedly, the study's sample of forty students is small, and all of them came from one school. ______, the improvement appeared in every one of the four classrooms tested, which chance alone would rarely produce.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence grants the weakness but argues the result remains meaningful, which 'still' conveys.
items.skill_note: Concede and counter. The consistency across classrooms does not follow from the small sample.

items.passage: The fungus attacks only trees already stressed by drought. ______, the die-off was worst along the ridge, where the soil is thinnest and dries first.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The ridge damage matches the prediction entailed by the fungus's preference, so the blank marks a consequence drawn from that fact.
items.skill_note: The second sentence is where you would expect damage given the first. That is inference, not illustration.

items.passage: The trial drew its volunteers from people who had already signed up for a fitness program. ______, the effect held even among the subset who reported never exercising before the study began.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A possible objection is raised and then answered, so the blank marks concession followed by persistence of the effect.
items.skill_note: The second sentence grants the weakness and says the result survives it.

items.passage: The two astronomers published within weeks of each other, and neither had seen the other's work. ______, their estimates of the comet's orbital period differ by less than a day.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Independent work that nonetheless agrees is a mild contrast with expectation, which 'nevertheless' marks.
items.skill_note: Independence would lead you to expect disagreement; the agreement is a qualified surprise.

items.passage: The vaccine must be stored at minus seventy degrees, which few rural clinics can manage. ______, a freeze-dried version that survives at room temperature is now in late-stage trials.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The new formulation is a response to the storage problem, so the blank marks a consequence that follows from the constraint.
items.skill_note: A constraint provokes a technical response. 'Likewise' would make the new version a parallel case instead.

items.passage: The Romans lined their aqueduct channels with a volcanic cement that hardened underwater and resisted frost. ______, nineteenth-century engineers in the same region used portland cement, which cracked in the first hard winter.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Two engineering choices are compared in the same setting, so the blank marks a parallel case.
items.skill_note: Careful: the outcomes differ, but the sentences compare practices, and 'similarly' introduces the parallel practice, not an agreement in results.

items.passage: The trial enrolled only forty patients, all from a single clinic, and followed them for six months. ______, the improvement was consistent across every age group and every dose tested.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence concedes the limitations but argues the consistency is still meaningful, which 'even so' marks.
items.skill_note: Limitations acknowledged, conclusion defended. Not a consequence of the limitations.

items.passage: The restoration team cleaned the fresco with lasers rather than solvents. ______, conservators at a nearby site used a poultice of ammonium carbonate, with results that took four years to stabilize.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: A parallel conservation effort in another location is offered for comparison, so the blank marks similarity of situation.
items.skill_note: Both are cleaning methods; the differences in outcome do not cancel the parallel.

items.passage: A nutrition researcher claims that drinking coffee within four hours of bedtime does not affect sleep quality in healthy adults.
items.stem:
Participants were given coffee or a placebo four hours before bedtime.

Group | Minutes to fall asleep (min)
---|---
Placebo | 14
Coffee | 27

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the claim?
choices: Coffee drinkers took 27  min to fall asleep against 14  min for the placebo group, and they woke more often during the night.
The study was conducted in a sleep laboratory over two nights.
Coffee drinkers reported enjoying the taste of the beverage.
Participants were asked to keep their usual bedtime.
items.explanation: A doubled time to fall asleep plus more awakenings directly contradicts the claim that sleep quality is unaffected.
items.skill_note: Taste and setting describe the experiment, not its result.

items.passage: A health system claims that its telehealth program, which lets patients see a clinician by video instead of traveling to a clinic, reduced missed appointments among patients with chronic conditions.
items.stem:
Rates for the two visit types appear in the table.

Visit type | Missed appointment rate (%)
---|---
In person | 19
Telehealth | 7

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the claim?
choices: The program was launched in three rural counties.
Telehealth visits were missed 7% of the time against 19% for in-person visits, among patients matched on condition and age.
Patients could join telehealth visits by telephone as well as video.
Clinicians reported spending less time on documentation.
items.explanation: A twelve-point gap in the missed-appointment rate, among matched patients, is the outcome the claim names.
items.skill_note: Access by telephone explains how patients attended, not whether they did.

items.passage: A restoration team proposed that shading newly planted seedlings with a permeable cloth would raise first-year survival on a dry hillside by reducing evaporation from the soil surface. They planted 200 seedlings of the same species on the same slope, half under cloth and half in the open, and counted survivors after one dry season.
items.stem:
The results appear in the table.

Treatment | Surviving after one dry season (%)
---|---
Open | 41
Shaded | 68

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the team's proposal?
choices: Open seedlings were browsed by deer in three of the ten plots.
Shaded seedlings grew 12 centimeters taller on average than open seedlings.
The cloth cost about forty cents per square meter and lasted two seasons.
Shaded seedlings survived at 68%, against 41% among seedlings left unshaded.
items.explanation: The proposal is specifically about survival, and the table shows a 27-point survival advantage for shaded seedlings in a controlled comparison on one slope.
items.skill_note: Growth, cost, and browsing are separate outcomes; only the survival difference tests the proposal.

items.passage: A fertilizer company claims its slow-release pellets raise wheat yields by at least twenty percent over conventional fertilizer. An agronomist tested the claim on twelve fields, applying the two products at the same nitrogen rate.
items.stem:
Results from the twelve fields appear in the table.

Fertilizer | Mean yield (t/ha)
---|---
Conventional | 6.4
Slow-release | 6.6

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the company's claim?
choices: Slow-release pellets reduced nitrogen runoff into a nearby stream.
Slow-release plots averaged 6.6  t/ha against 6.4  t/ha for Conventional plots, a difference of about 0.2  t/ha.
The company's pellets dissolved more evenly across the season.
The slow-release pellets cost roughly twice as much per hectare.
items.explanation: A 0.2 t/ha difference is about three percent, far short of the twenty percent claimed, so the yield data directly undercut the claim.
items.skill_note: The claim is quantitative; only a yield comparison can test it.

items.passage: A curator argues that the foreign-looking pottery found at a coastal settlement was made locally by potters copying imported styles, not brought in by traders.
items.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the curator's argument?
choices: Chemical analysis shows the pots' clay matches a riverbed two kilometers from the settlement, and their tempers include crushed shell found only on that coast.
The settlement's harbor handled goods from three regions.
Similar shapes appear at inland sites along the same river.
The pots were found in houses rather than in a storage building.
items.explanation: Local clay and local shell temper place the manufacture at the settlement, which is exactly what the curator claims.
items.skill_note: A busy harbor and inland parallels are consistent with trade; they do not identify where the pots were made.

items.passage: An advocacy group claims that mailing every registered voter a ballot raises turnout, and points to a state that adopted universal mail voting in 2020.
items.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the group's claim?
choices: The state's turnout had been rising gradually since 2008.
Most voters in the state said they found the instructions clear.
Turnout in that state rose eleven points in 2020 while turnout in four similar states without mail voting rose two points, and the gap persisted in the next two elections.
Mail ballots were counted more slowly than in-person ballots.
items.explanation: A large gain relative to comparable states, sustained across elections, isolates the voting method from statewide trends.
items.skill_note: A pre-existing upward trend actually undercuts the claim; only the comparison supports it.

items.passage: A school district adopted a new mathematics curriculum in all of its middle schools and announced that test scores had risen by nine points, crediting the curriculum.
items.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the district's conclusion?
choices: Middle schools in the same state that did not adopt the curriculum also gained nine points, and the district's gain was concentrated in the year the state shortened its test.
The district spent two million dollars on new textbooks.
Teachers attended forty hours of training before the curriculum began.
Parents reported that their children enjoyed mathematics more.
items.explanation: A gain of the same size without the curriculum, plus a change in the test itself, leaves nothing for the curriculum to explain.
items.skill_note: Implementation effort shows the program was real; it does not show the program caused the gain.

items.passage: An ecologist proposes that a desert shrub depends on nectar-feeding bats, rather than on bees, for pollination, because its flowers open only at night and produce a scent strongest after dark.
items.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the proposal?
choices: The shrub grows in the same habitat as three species of bat.
The shrub's flowers contain more nectar than those of neighboring species.
Shrubs enclosed in mesh that admits bees but excludes bats set almost no seed, while open shrubs and shrubs hand-pollinated at night set seed normally.
Bees visit the flowers briefly at dawn, after the scent has faded.
items.explanation: Excluding bats alone collapses seed set, which is a direct experimental test of dependence on bat pollination.
items.skill_note: Nectar volume and shared habitat suggest a relationship without testing it.

items.passage: A district claims that its new after-school reading program raised comprehension scores for struggling readers in grades three to five.
items.stem:
Students were assigned to the program by lottery among those who applied.

Group | Mean gain in comprehension score (points)
---|---
Not selected | 3.1
Selected | 7.8

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the district's claim?
choices: The program ran three afternoons a week for twenty weeks.
Students selected by lottery gained 7.8  points against 3.1  points for applicants not selected, a gap of 4.7 points.
Ninety percent of parents said they would enroll their child again.
The program was paid for by a state literacy grant.
items.explanation: A lottery comparison isolates the program from family motivation, and the gap is the direct measure the claim requires.
items.skill_note: Satisfaction and hours describe the program's delivery, not its effect.

items.passage: A fitness company reports that its app increases weekly exercise, citing a survey in which users reported exercising more after downloading it.
items.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the company's claim?
choices: The app's subscription costs eight dollars a month.
Some users said the app's reminders were annoying.
Users who paid for the premium tier exercised more than free users.
Users who downloaded the app were already exercising twice as much as non-users before downloading it, and their weekly minutes did not change afterward.
items.explanation: A pre-existing difference plus no change after download means the survey compared different people rather than measuring an effect.
